evidence.quote: This voluntary framework provides a flexible, structured, and measurable process to address AI risks throughout the AI lifecycle

Appropriate methods and metrics are identified and applied... Approaches and metrics for quantitative or qualitative measurement of the enumerated risks... are identified and selected for implementation.
Practical approaches for AI safety often relate to rigorous simulation and in-domain testing, real-time monitoring, and the ability to quickly shut down or modify misbehaving systems.
deploying the system in production environments subject to increased testing or other controls

Transparency reflects the extent to which information is available to a user when interacting with an AI system. Its scope spans from design decisions and training data to model training, the structure of the model, its intended use case
Explainable systems can be more easily debugged and monitored, and lend themselves to more thorough documentation, audit, and governance.
input from a broad and diverse set of stakeholders is required throughout the AI lifecycle to ensure that risks arising in social contexts are managed appropriately
Individual human operators and their organizations should be answerable and held accountable for the outcomes of AI systems
This voluntary framework provides a flexible, structured, and measurable process to address AI risks throughout the AI lifecycle
It is important to note that the AI RMF is neither a checklist nor should be used in any way to certify an AI system.
using the AI RMF does not substitute for due diligence and judgment by organizations and individuals in deciding whether to design, develop, and deploy AI technologies
